text:
alex: Quick FYI — noticed a p95 regression in nightly after the arch-aware pick change. +30% on some seq-length tails.
priya: Ugh, which flows? short vs long sequences? any env flags to repro locally?
ajex: short-ish sequences (~32-80 tokens) on avx2 instances. Long seqs look fine. repro on rdw-integ with small batch sizes.
alex: Repro steps: set REDWOOD_KERNEL_DECISION_EXPLAIN=1 and REDWOOD_KERNEL_TRACE=1, then run ./bench --model=gpt-small --seq=48 --batch=2. Logs attached below.
priya: Can you paste the decision snippet instead of full logs?
alex: Sure — here's the pick lines we saw:

```
[2026-03-15T08:12:34Z] kpick: model=gpt-small, arch=skx, seq_bucket=32-64, chosen=gemm_fast, reason=estimated_latency(11.4ms) vs alt=kv_fused(12.1ms)
[2026-03-15T08:12:34Z] kpick: profile: kv_hit=false, batch=2, kv_cache_sz=0, memory_available=11.2GB
[2026-03-15T08:12:34Z] kpick: fallback_path=gemm_safe if gemm_fast fails; debug_flags=RDW_PICK_LOG=1,RDW_PROFILE_BUCKETS=8
```

priya: Hmm that looks fine, but production telemetry shows many 'chosen=gemm_fast' on avx2 and p95 went up. Any change in fallback timing?
jordan: I pushed a micro-opt that changed the cost model: we added a fixed overhead for small batches to favor fused kernels. Maybe the overhead calc is wrong for AVX2.
marta: If the cost model over-weights kernel setup, it can flip picks for the 32-64 bucket. We should compare cost components (setup vs per-token).
alex: I dumped the telemetry envelope from perf-bot for the failing window. Snippet below:

```
{
  "ts": 1801234500,
  "model": "gpt-small",
  "arch": "skx",
  "seq_bucket": "32-64",
  "chosen": "gemm_fast",
  "reason_bits": ["est_latency","arch_hint"],
  "cost_components": {"setup_ms":"6.3","per_token_ms":"0.1","kv_adj_ms":"0.0"},
  "observed_p95_ms": "15.4"
}
```

sam: Observed_p95 15.4 vs estimated 11.4 — that gap explains the regression. Either cost model wrong or runtime overhead (cache warm, memory thrash).
priya: Can we enable RDW_KERNEL_PROFILE=seq_buckets on canary, collect cost_components per-request and run a delta? Also add RDW_KERNEL_LOG_FAULTS=1 to capture fallback triggers.
jordan: I'll roll a canary with RDW_KERNEL_PROFILE=seq_buckets, RDW_KERNEL_DECISION_EXPLAIN=1, RDW_KERNEL_LOG_FAULTS=1 to a 5% traffic slice.
marta: Also instrument batching heuristics: BATCH_HEUR_DEBUG=1 so we can see if batch shaping is causing smaller than expected batches.
alex: One more: kv behavior matters — if kv_hit=true, fused kernels win. Perf traces showed kv_hit=false on production for that time window. Maybe KV cache warm strategy changed.
perf-bot: noted — created perf/1801234567 for the investigation, ingest hooks active.
priya: Plan: collect traces for 24h, then run offline replayer with both old/new cost code to compare picks and observed latencies. Jordan, can you keep the canary for 6h and then bump to 24h if initial diffs look stable?
jordan: Yup — starting canary now. Will post initial telemetry snapshot in ~30m.
alex: Thanks. If anyone can look at the cost calc in kselect/cost_model.cc — I suspect the setup_ms term got a factor of 2 by mistake.
marta: I'll throw a tiny unit test that asserts cost_model(setup_ms) unchanged for batch<=4.
priya: Excellent. Keep logs short and paste the explanatory pick lines only. Use the flags above when posting. :thumbsup:
